paragraphs: Multi-view stereo estimates scene depth from several images. This paper proposes a framework that does not require a predefined depth range and considers all source images together. That distinguishes its approach from prior range-free methods that process image pairs, allowing information from multiple views to participate in the same estimation process.

Its Multi-view Disparity Attention module combines information across distant image locations and across views. Camera geometry matters because corresponding points are constrained by how the cameras observe the scene. The method embeds camera poses into its representations, supplying implicit geometric guidance for attention when combining disparity features.

The framework also accounts for differences in how well each source image observes a reference pixel. It maintains separate hidden states for source images, estimates the quality of candidate correspondences along epipolar lines, and updates those states using uncertainty estimates. Results on DTU and Tanks&Temple support the method’s effectiveness. The contribution combines joint multi-view reasoning, pose information, and changing estimates of observation quality without requiring a depth-range prior.
neurips-2024-a-global-depth-range-free-m.tldr: A depth-range-free stereo network combines all source views using pose-guided attention and uncertainty-aware updates.

paragraphs: AsCAN addresses the challenge of designing a neural network architecture that works across different visual tasks while balancing performance and execution time. The paper combines convolutional blocks and transformer blocks in a hybrid architecture, with the aim of making the same basic design useful for both recognition and generation.

The central design choice is an asymmetric distribution of the two block types. Earlier stages contain more convolutional blocks, while later stages contain more transformer blocks. The contribution therefore concerns where these components appear within the network, as well as their combination. The authors apply this arrangement to recognition, segmentation, and image generation conditioned on a class.

The reported results show a favorable performance–latency trade-off across these tasks. The authors also scale the architecture to large-scale text-to-image generation, reporting state-of-the-art performance against the public and commercial models they compare. Their model executes faster in those comparisons without additional inference-time optimization, including comparisons with optimized systems. These findings support architectural allocation as a useful route to efficient, broadly reusable visual models.
neurips-2024-ascan-asymmetric-convolutio.tldr: AsCAN places more convolutional blocks early and more transformer blocks later to improve performance and latency across visual tasks.

paragraphs: CableInspect-AD examines whether visual anomaly detectors can handle the defects encountered during robotic power line inspection. Strong performance in controlled settings does not establish performance on the varied anomalies found in this application. The authors introduce a public dataset of high-resolution images created and annotated by Hydro-Québec domain experts, including defects with different severity levels.

The paper also modifies PatchCore to address a practical difficulty: collecting enough varied normal and anomalous examples to choose a detection threshold. The enhanced method supports settings with limited labeled data. A cross-validation evaluation protocol accompanies the dataset, providing a systematic way to assess model performance.

The evaluation covers Enhanced-PatchCore with few or many examples and vision-language models operating without task-specific labeled examples. Although the models show promise, they struggle to detect every anomaly represented in the data. This finding makes the dataset useful as a demanding benchmark: it exposes remaining detection difficulties in a concrete inspection setting, while providing expert annotations and an evaluation procedure for studying them.
neurips-2024-cableinspect-ad-an-expert-a.tldr: CableInspect-AD provides expert-labeled power line images that reveal persistent challenges for visual anomaly detectors.

paragraphs: This paper studies why language models can struggle to learn new facts from limited fine-tuning text. The authors identify a bias toward learning which words appear together rather than learning factual relationships that remain useful across different reasoning tasks. A model may consequently answer a straightforward question without applying the same knowledge successfully in a more indirect setting.

The study distinguishes two forms of representation. It associates co-occurrence statistics with middle transformer layers and factual associations with lower layers. In the reported analysis, the former transfer poorly beyond simple question answering, whereas the latter support varied reasoning tasks. This distinction motivates changes to how new knowledge is taught.

One strategy trains on text where factual associations are implicit, encouraging the model to learn the underlying relationship. Another actively makes the model forget learned co-occurrence statistics during training on narrative text. On synthetic and real-world corpora, both strategies improve the transfer of newly learned knowledge to indirect and multi-hop questions. The findings connect how knowledge is represented with whether fine-tuning produces reusable reasoning capabilities.
neurips-2024-co-occurrence-is-not-factua.tldr: Two training strategies improve factual generalization by reducing language models’ reliance on word co-occurrence statistics.

paragraphs: CulturePark addresses the shortage of culturally representative training data for language models. Building cultural datasets from existing collections, online platforms, and human annotations can be expensive and difficult to scale. The paper proposes generating cultural data through simulated communication between language-model agents assigned roles from different cultures.

These agents produce cross-cultural dialogues about beliefs, norms, and customs. Using this framework, the authors generate 41,000 samples and fine-tune eight culture-specific models. The approach makes simulated social interaction a source of training material, linking the data-generation process directly to the goal of improving models’ handling of cultural differences.

Evaluation covers content moderation, cultural alignment, and cultural education. The GPT-3.5-based models match or exceed GPT-4 on 41 content-moderation datasets and outperform it on the Hofstede VSM 13 cultural-alignment framework. In education involving human participants, they also produce better reported learning outcomes and user experiences than GPT-4. These results support the usefulness of the generated data for the evaluated tasks and measures, demonstrating a concrete way to improve cultural specialization through targeted fine-tuning.
neurips-2024-culturepark-boosting-cross-.tldr: CulturePark generates cross-cultural dialogues with language-model agents to train models that improve on evaluated cultural tasks.

paragraphs: Semi-supervised learning uses unlabeled examples to help learn from a limited labeled set. A difficulty arises when many unlabeled examples belong to classes absent from the labeled data. Existing methods often reduce the influence of these irrelevant examples, but doing so can also lose useful diversity and regularities contained in them.

This paper proposes using a diffusion model to generate additional labeled training data from both labeled and unlabeled samples. The challenge is to retain useful variation from the unlabeled collection while limiting synthetic examples that fall outside the target classes. The authors combine diffusion-model training with a discriminator that identifies irrelevant instances and reduces their influence.

The trained generator can even turn an irrelevant instance into a relevant one, according to the reported demonstrations. Experiments show substantial improvements to semi-supervised learning methods, especially when labeled and unlabeled class distributions differ. The contribution is a way to recover training value from a mismatched data collection through generation, rather than treating its usefulness solely as a decision about which original examples to emphasize.
neurips-2024-data-augmentation-with-diff.tldr: Discriminator-guided diffusion augmentation extracts useful diversity from mismatched unlabeled data to improve semi-supervised learning.

paragraphs: DCDepth estimates depth from a single image by changing the representation the model predicts. Conventional approaches estimate depth values in image space. This method instead represents patches of depth through discrete cosine coefficients, allowing it to model relationships among depth values within each patch.

The transformation separates broad structure from finer detail. Low-frequency components capture the main shape of the scene, while higher-frequency components describe more detailed variation. DCDepth uses this separation to organize prediction progressively: it first estimates low-frequency information to establish scene context, then predicts higher-frequency information to refine local details.

This ordering gives the model an explicit progression from overall structure to increasingly detailed depth estimates. The representation and prediction strategy work together: the frequency decomposition supplies the components, and the progressive procedure determines how they are estimated. Experiments on NYU-Depth-V2, TOFDC, and KITTI report state-of-the-art performance. The findings support predicting structured depth-patch coefficients as an effective alternative to conventional spatial-domain depth estimation in the evaluated datasets.
neurips-2024-dcdepth-progressive-monocul.tldr: DCDepth predicts depth-patch frequency coefficients progressively, establishing broad scene structure before refining detail.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether AI teammates actually collaborate with people in Overcooked-AI. The authors find that leading imitation-learning and reinforcement-learning approaches are brittle and tend to separate human and machine actions so the machine can operate independently. That behavior falls short of the mutually coordinated teamwork the study seeks.

The proposed approaches let users iteratively develop their AI teammates through mixed-initiative interaction. In particular, people can inspect and interactively reprogram interpretable agents. A study with 50 participants examines how these design choices affect team development and performance, including the relationship between understandable models and the ability to modify them.

A central negative result is that every tested approach underperforms a simple collaborative heuristic. Within those comparisons, interactive modification improves team development over interpretable models alone, while black-box approaches are easier to train and deliver better teaming performance. The findings expose a trade-off among explainability, interactivity, and training ease. They motivate better collaborative learning methods, stronger interpretable agents, and interfaces that help users with different abilities improve teamwork.
neurips-2024-designs-for-enabling-collab.tldr: A human–AI teaming study finds benefits from interactive agent modification, but all tested approaches trail a simple collaborative heuristic.

paragraphs: Drones Help Drones studies how multiple drones can combine their observations to predict object motion. Different views provide complementary information, but broad aerial scenes make accurate bird’s-eye representations difficult. Communication is another constraint: exchanging too much information can conflict with the bandwidth and timing requirements of drone-based prediction.

The framework addresses both problems. It uses ground-related information from inclined drone views to estimate object-to-drone distances and improve bird’s-eye representations. It also compares local features to select important information for communication, prioritizing exchanges that contribute to the prediction task. The authors introduce Air-Co-Pred as the first dataset for multi-drone collaborative prediction.

Experiments report more than a 20% reduction in positional deviation in bird’s-eye representations relative to state-of-the-art approaches. The framework also achieves comparable prediction performance using only one quarter of the transmission ratio. These results connect better geometric representations with more selective communication. Further experiments on CoPerception-UAVs show promising transfer to collaborative 3D object detection, suggesting the approach may be useful beyond trajectory prediction.
neurips-2024-drones-help-drones-a-collab.tldr: DHD improves multi-drone geometry and selectively shares features to maintain trajectory prediction performance with less communication.

paragraphs: Dynamic Neural Regeneration addresses training deep networks when only a small dataset is available. The paper builds on iterative training methods that reset some model parameters to improve generalization. Earlier approaches often choose those parameters randomly and keep the selection mask fixed, which may leave the reset process poorly matched to what the network is learning.

DNR instead uses a changing, data-aware mask. It estimates the significance of connections and uses that information to identify redundant ones. Randomly reinitializing selected weights then creates capacity for further learning. The important distinction is that randomness remains in the replacement weights, while the choice of connections responds to the data and their estimated importance.

The authors report better accuracy and robustness than existing methods in their experiments. These findings support adapting the regeneration process during training rather than relying on a fixed selection of parameters. The approach is motivated by neurogenesis in the brain, but its concrete contribution is a training procedure that combines significance-based selection with repeated weight renewal for learning from limited data.
neurips-2024-dynamic-neural-regeneration.tldr: Dynamic Neural Regeneration uses data-aware connection selection and weight resets to improve small-dataset accuracy and robustness.

paragraphs: Neighborhood attention limits each token to nearby tokens, reducing the computation associated with unrestricted attention. Yet a theoretically cheaper attention pattern can remain slow when its implementation moves too much data or performs operations inefficiently. This paper focuses on that implementation gap, particularly for attention over multidimensional inputs.

The authors first express neighborhood attention as batched matrix multiplication and build kernels for one- and two-dimensional cases. These improve runtime over naive CUDA implementations, but unfused implementations retain memory-bandwidth bottlenecks and other inefficiencies. The second approach adapts fused dot-product attention kernels, adding fine-grained control over attention along different spatial axes.

The fused kernels avoid some inefficiencies that remain in the unfused approach and deliver substantially stronger reported half-precision runtime improvements. At the model level, the authors report improvements of up to 104% for inference and 39% for training existing neighborhood-attention models. The work shows why restricting attention alone is insufficient to realize its practical efficiency benefits: the computational organization must also fit the hardware. The implementation further extends applicability to image and video perception.
neurips-2024-faster-neighborhood-attenti.tldr: New matrix-multiplication and fused kernels turn neighborhood attention’s theoretical savings into faster training and inference.

paragraphs: Cross-domain recommendation uses information from other domains to improve recommendations where data are sparse. Sharing information introduces two problems addressed by FedGCDR: protecting privacy during transfer and avoiding negative transfer, where source-domain knowledge harms the target model. These concerns become especially relevant when several source domains contribute information.

FedGCDR combines federated graph attention networks with a positive knowledge transfer module. This module uses differential privacy-based extraction and feature mapping to turn source embeddings into transferable domain knowledge. A separate knowledge activation module filters information that may be harmful or conflict with the target domain.

The activation process expands the target-domain graph to produce domain attentions and fine-tunes the target model to improve filtering and prediction. Thus, knowledge transfer includes both a privacy-oriented extraction step and a relevance-oriented selection step. Experiments across 16 Amazon domains report significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods. The findings support jointly addressing privacy and the quality of transferred information when using multiple domains to strengthen recommendation models.
neurips-2024-federated-graph-learning-fo.tldr: FedGCDR combines privacy-preserving knowledge transfer with harmful-knowledge filtering to improve cross-domain recommendations.

paragraphs: HEALNet addresses how to combine biomedical data whose forms differ substantially, including images, tables, and graphs. Many multimodal systems process each source with a separate architecture, often trained independently. This can prevent them from capturing the interactions between data sources that make combining those sources valuable.

The proposed architecture uses early attention-based fusion while preserving structure specific to each modality. It learns shared internal representations that capture cross-modal interactions alongside structural information. It also works directly with raw inputs rather than opaque embeddings, supporting model inspection. Handling missing modalities during both training and inference is an explicit part of the design.

The authors evaluate HEALNet on survival analysis using whole-slide images and multi-omic data from four TCGA cancer datasets. They report state-of-the-art performance among the compared end-to-end fusion models, substantial improvements over single-modality and multimodal baselines, and robustness when modalities are missing. These results support a fusion strategy that learns relationships across data sources while retaining their distinctive structure and accommodating incomplete inputs.
neurips-2024-healnet-multimodal-fusion-f.tldr: HEALNet combines heterogeneous biomedical inputs through early attention-based fusion and remains robust when some modalities are missing.

paragraphs: LLM-AutoDA addresses learning from long-tailed data, where some classes have many examples and others have relatively few. Existing approaches use rebalancing or augmentation to reduce this difficulty, but augmentation strategies may be manually designed, drawn from a restricted search space, or held fixed throughout training.

The framework uses a large pretrained language model to search automatically for augmentation strategies suited to the imbalanced data. It applies a proposed strategy to produce an augmented dataset and then fine-tunes the underlying learning model. Improvement on a validation set becomes a reward signal for updating the strategy-generation model.

This creates an iterative feedback loop: the effects of one augmentation proposal guide the generation of subsequent proposals. The strategy can therefore evolve according to measured learning performance instead of remaining unchanged. Across multiple established long-tailed benchmarks, the authors report significant gains over state-of-the-art augmentation and rebalancing methods. The results support using a language model as an adaptive augmentation designer, with validation feedback connecting its proposals to the needs of the downstream learner.
neurips-2024-llm-autoda-large-language-m.tldr: LLM-AutoDA uses validation rewards to iteratively improve language-model-generated augmentation strategies for imbalanced datasets.

paragraphs: LoTLIP studies how language–image pretraining can better handle long descriptions. The authors empirically identify short training captions as a key cause of weak long-text understanding: prominent tokens can overshadow other textual information. Simply replacing short captions with longer ones does not fully solve the problem, because it can reduce performance on short-text tasks such as image classification.

The proposed approach adds corner tokens that aggregate diverse textual information. With these tokens, the model recovers its original short-text understanding while substantially improving its handling of long text. The intervention therefore addresses both the richer training descriptions and the model’s ability to collect information from them.

The authors further examine increasing caption length and observe a clear trade-off between performance and efficiency. They validate the approach on a self-constructed collection of 100 million image–text pairs oriented toward long captions, reporting superior long-text image retrieval performance. The findings show that benefiting from richer descriptions depends on how textual information is aggregated, alongside the amount of text provided during training.
neurips-2024-lotlip-improving-language-i.tldr: LoTLIP combines long captions with information-aggregating corner tokens to improve long-text image understanding while recovering short-text performance.

paragraphs: This paper studies whether language models can accurately recall a graph described in earlier text. Such recall matters because reasoning about relationships depends on retaining the underlying network of connections. The authors examine both overall accuracy and local structural biases, drawing motivation from research on patterned errors in human graph recall.

The study finds that language models often perform poorly at reconstructing these graphs. Their recalled structures also favor particular patterns, including triangles and alternating two-paths. These are structural tendencies in the reconstructed relationships, making the investigation more specific than an assessment of how many individual connections are remembered correctly.

The authors also find that more advanced models’ recall depends strongly on the domain of a real-world graph. Accuracy is highest when the narrative style matches the graph’s original domain. This means that the presentation of relationships can affect whether the model preserves them faithfully. Together, the findings identify both local structural preferences and domain-sensitive recall as features to consider when assessing language models’ ability to work with graph information expressed in text.
neurips-2024-microstructures-and-accurac.tldr: Language models exhibit biased local structures in graph recall, with advanced models recalling best when narrative style matches the graph’s domain.

paragraphs: Predict+Optimize learns predictions for parameters that an optimization problem needs but that are not known when decisions must be made. This paper extends that framework to situations where information arrives in stages, with decisions occurring between revelations. Such a setting gives later predictions access to information unavailable at the beginning.

The authors develop three neural-network training algorithms for mixed integer linear programs. The first extends earlier work by using one network to make a single prediction of the unknown parameters. The other two use a separate network at each stage, allowing predictions to change as additional information becomes available.

Training the stage-specific networks requires handling their interdependence: decisions and predictions at different stages belong to the same overall problem. The authors use sequential and parallelized forms of coordinate descent to manage these dependencies. Experiments on three benchmarks report superior learning performance over classical approaches. The contribution is a framework and proof-of-concept algorithms that explicitly incorporate the timing of information, allowing prediction and optimization to adapt across a sequence of decisions.
neurips-2024-multi-stage-predict-optimiz.tldr: Multi-Stage Predict+Optimize updates predictions as information arrives between optimization decisions.

paragraphs: Johnson–Lindenstrauss embeddings provide compact representations with strong guarantees for preserving distances. Standard randomized methods offer essentially unimprovable worst-case guarantees, but neither their algorithms nor their analyses exploit possible structure in a particular dataset. This paper asks whether optimization directly informed by the data can provide another route.

The authors first establish an obstacle: optimizing the distance-preservation objective directly over projection matrices produces a nonconvex landscape with many bad stationary points. Their proposed method changes the space being optimized. Inspired by diffusion models, it optimizes over random solution samplers rather than individual projection matrices and gradually reduces the sampler’s variance.

The paper shows that optimization through this larger space converges to a deterministic solution with zero variance while avoiding bad stationary points. Randomness therefore serves as part of the route to a final deterministic embedding. The authors interpret the method as optimization-based derandomization and suggest that the idea could extend to other problems. That broader applicability is presented as a possibility, while the stated result concerns the embedding objective studied here.
neurips-2024-optimization-can-learn-john.tldr: Optimizing over random solution samplers and shrinking their variance yields deterministic embeddings while avoiding bad stationary points.

paragraphs: This paper studies scheduling when jobs arrive randomly into multiple queues and servers have unknown service behavior. A scheduler assigns jobs to servers, but each server serves at most one assigned job, chosen stochastically according to its preferences. The service rates follow a feature-based multinomial logit model.

The learning challenge is coupled to queue management. The scheduler must discover which assignments work well while preventing waiting jobs from accumulating without control. The authors propose algorithms based on upper confidence bounds and Thompson sampling, combining learning about service behavior with the objective of stabilizing the system.

For sufficiently long time horizons, the algorithms achieve stability with average queue length bounded in order by the smaller of the queue and server counts divided by traffic slackness. The guarantee thus depends explicitly on the system’s spare capacity. The authors also establish sublinear regret bounds involving the time horizon and maximum queue length, and provide experimental results. Together, the results characterize learning performance and congestion control under the stated preference-based service model.
neurips-2024-queueing-matching-bandits-w.tldr: Preference-aware bandit schedulers learn unknown service rates while providing queue-stability and sublinear-regret guarantees.

paragraphs: This paper considers reinforcement learning where an agent sees realized rewards or transitions at its current state before choosing an action. Such lookahead information changes the decision problem because the agent can respond to observations that ordinary action selection does not use. Previous work established large benefits when the environment is already known.

The authors address unknown environments by designing learning algorithms that incorporate these observations. Their planning procedure uses the empirical distribution of observed rewards and transitions, rather than relying only on estimated expectations. This retains distributional information needed to plan decisions that depend on what the agent gets to observe before acting.

The theoretical comparison uses a baseline that also receives lookahead information. This is significant because it evaluates learning against a decision-maker with the same informational advantage. The authors prove tight regret guarantees and report a linear increase in collected reward relative to agents that cannot handle lookahead information. The contribution is an efficient learning framework tailored to this observation structure, extending the usefulness of lookahead beyond settings where the environment is known in advance.
neurips-2024-reinforcement-learning-with.tldr: Distribution-based planning enables provably efficient reinforcement learning when reward or transition realizations are visible before action selection.

paragraphs: ReST-MCTS* addresses a weakness in language-model self-training: a response can end with the correct answer while containing faulty plans or intermediate reasoning. Filtering generated responses by final-answer correctness can therefore produce poor training traces. The paper combines process-level reward guidance with tree search to improve the reasoning data collected.

Given oracle correct final answers, the method estimates how likely an intermediate step is to help reach the correct answer. These estimates supply step-level rewards without manual annotation of each step. They serve two purposes: training the process reward model and selecting higher-quality reasoning traces for training the policy model.

The reported tree-search policy achieves higher accuracy than Best-of-N and Tree-of-Thought under the same search budget. Using its traces for self-training also improves three language models across multiple iterations and outperforms ReST EM and Self-Rewarding LM in the reported comparisons. The results support a feedback loop in which search improves training traces and inferred step values refine reward guidance. Access to oracle final answers is an explicit condition of that process.
neurips-2024-rest-mcts-llm-self-training.tldr: ReST-MCTS* uses answer-supervised tree search to infer step rewards and generate better reasoning traces for iterative self-training.

paragraphs: This paper studies how variational quantum algorithms can respect hard constraints while operating on noisy quantum devices. Incorporating such constraints is an open challenge for these algorithms. The authors combine a Hamming Weight Preserving ansatz, a parameterized circuit structure, with a parity check that accounts for the topology of the physical qubits.

The combination brings constraint preservation and error mitigation into the same approach. The circuit preserves Hamming weight, while the topology-aware parity check supports error mitigation and further hard constraints. This makes the relationship between circuit design and physical-qubit structure central to the proposed method.

The authors evaluate the combination on quantum chemistry and constrained combinatorial optimization problems, including the Quadratic Assignment Problem. Experiments use both simulators and superconducting quantum processors and show significant improvements over peer variational quantum methods. These findings support the combination as a promising candidate for pursuing quantum advantage on more realistic problems in the noisy intermediate-scale setting. The stated conclusion is prospective: the results establish comparative performance in the studied tasks and motivate further pursuit of quantum advantage.
neurips-2024-rethinking-parity-check-enh.tldr: Combining a Hamming-weight-preserving quantum circuit with topology-aware parity checks improves constrained-task performance in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Safe LoRA addresses the safety degradation that can accompany language-model fine-tuning, including fine-tuning on data without malicious content. LoRA makes customization less computationally demanding by updating a limited parameterization, but this efficiency does not itself protect the model’s safety behavior. The paper proposes a small modification to the LoRA implementation.

The method projects LoRA weights from selected layers into a safety-aligned subspace. It requires the weights of both the base model and its aligned counterpart. The safety intervention is training-free and data-free, so applying it does not require an additional training procedure or a separate dataset.

In experiments using purely malicious fine-tuning data, Safe LoRA retains safety performance similar to the original aligned model. With a mixture of benign and malicious data, it reduces the harmful effect of malicious examples while preserving downstream task performance. These findings support weight projection as a practical means of reducing fine-tuning risks while maintaining utility. The evidence concerns the reported experimental settings and establishes risk reduction rather than a universal guarantee of safe behavior.
neurips-2024-safe-lora-the-silver-lining.tldr: Safe LoRA projects selected adaptation weights into a safety-aligned subspace to reduce fine-tuning risks while preserving utility.

paragraphs: SearchLVLMs addresses visual questions that require knowledge newer than a vision-language model’s training. Frequently updating large models is resource-intensive, so the framework supplies current internet information during inference. Its plug-and-play design augments existing models by adding relevant searched content to the information they receive.

The main component is a trained hierarchical filtering model that selects useful material from websites returned by a search engine. This matters because retrieving pages alone does not identify which content helps answer a particular visual question. To train and evaluate the framework, the authors build UDK-VQA through an automated pipeline that creates news-related visual question-answering samples.

A multi-model voting mechanism labels how useful websites and their contents are for those samples, supplying supervision for filtering. Experiments demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness and report approximately 30% higher accuracy than GPT-4o. The stated percentage does not specify a percentage-point interpretation. The contribution connects current-information retrieval, learned content selection, and automatically generated evaluation data in a framework for questions whose answers depend on recent knowledge.
neurips-2024-searchlvlms-a-plug-and-play.tldr: SearchLVLMs filters internet search results to help existing vision-language models answer questions requiring current knowledge.

paragraphs: This paper studies contextual bandits with graph feedback. Choosing an action reveals rewards for neighboring actions in a feedback graph across all contexts, giving the learner information beyond the chosen action. The authors investigate how this richer feedback structure and the number of contexts jointly determine learning difficulty.

They introduce a graph quantity, beta_M(G), and establish a regret lower bound proportional to the square root of beta_M(G) times the time horizon. As the context count changes, this quantity interpolates between the graph’s independence number and its maximum acyclic subgraph number. The result connects two different structural descriptions of the feedback graph through contextual complexity.

The authors also provide algorithms with near-optimal regret for important classes of context sequences or feedback graphs, including transitively closed graphs relevant to auctions and inventory control. With many contexts, their results identify the maximum acyclic subgraph number as the essential statistical-complexity measure, contrasting with the independence number’s role in multi-armed bandits. The contribution therefore clarifies both a fundamental learning limit and settings where algorithms nearly attain it.
neurips-2024-stochastic-contextual-bandi.tldr: A new graph quantity characterizes contextual-bandit learning limits and connects independence number to maximum acyclic subgraph number.
